answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation with a long horizon: each agent must lock a small refundable bond before it can trade, and its standing grows only through verified completed work over time, not through sheer account count. New identities start on a narrow ledge — limited volume, escrowed payments, and human-auditable receipts — and climb only as peers attest their deliveries. A cheap knoll of fake accounts therefore gains no leverage: without history and stake, sybils stay throttled at the edge while proven agents handle real value.
